exam.name: Kerala PSC Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Medical Education

title.en: Applied anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, embryology & pathology
Cardiac investigations (ECG, X-ray, echo, cath, CT/MRI, PET, CAD physiology)
Genetics and gene therapy in CVD
Atherosclerotic heart disease: ACS and CCS
Congenital heart disease: cyanotic and acyanotic
Arrhythmia management and sudden cardiac death
Prosthetic valve disease and percutaneous valve replacement
Cardiac evaluation for non-cardiac surgery and anaesthesia

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Coronary dominance is set by which artery gives the posterior descending artery (PDA). About 70% of people are right-dominant.

why.en: The PDA supplies the inferior septum, so dominance predicts which occlusion causes an inferior infarct.

recall_q.en: What decides coronary dominance?

recall_a.en: The artery that gives the posterior descending artery.

explain_simple.en: Follow the PDA back to its parent: RCA means right-dominant, circumflex means left-dominant, both means co-dominant.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: The SA nodal artery comes from the RCA in about 60% and the circumflex in about 40%. The AV nodal artery usually comes from the dominant artery.

why.en: So inferior MI from RCA occlusion often causes sinus bradycardia and AV block.

recall_q.en: Which artery usually supplies the AV node?

recall_a.en: The dominant artery, usually the RCA.

explain_simple.en: RCA blockage often slows the heart because the RCA usually feeds the AV node.

example.en: A patient with inferior STEMI develops complete heart block that often resolves after RCA reperfusion.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Left ventricular myocardium is perfused mainly in diastole.

why.en: Systolic contraction compresses intramyocardial vessels; tachycardia shortens diastole and reduces coronary flow.

recall_q.en: In which phase does the LV receive most coronary flow?

explain_simple.en: The squeezing ventricle pinches its own arteries, so blood flows in when it relaxes. Faster heart rate means less relaxing time.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Frank–Starling law: a larger end-diastolic volume (preload) gives a stronger contraction, up to a limit.

why.en: Stretch brings actin and myosin to better overlap and raises troponin C calcium sensitivity.

recall_q.en: What does the Frank–Starling law relate?

explain_simple.en: More filling stretches the muscle like a rubber band, so it springs back harder, until it is overstretched in failure.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: The ductus arteriosus comes from the left sixth aortic arch and closes functionally within the first few days after birth.

why.en: Rising oxygen and falling prostaglandin E2 after birth constrict it; so PGE1 infusion keeps it open in duct-dependent lesions.

recall_q.en: Which drug keeps the ductus arteriosus open?

explain_simple.en: Before birth prostaglandins hold the duct open. After birth they fall and the duct shuts. Giving PGE1 holds it open again.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Digoxin inhibits the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium and contractility; it also increases vagal tone, slowing AV conduction.

why.en: Hypokalaemia increases digoxin toxicity because potassium competes with digoxin at the pump.

recall_q.en: Which electrolyte disturbance worsens digoxin toxicity?

explain_simple.en: Digoxin blocks the sodium pump, so less calcium leaves the cell and the heart squeezes harder. Low potassium lets more digoxin bind.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Free-wall rupture after MI is most likely about 3–7 days after infarction.

why.en: Macrophages are removing necrotic muscle and scar has not formed, so the wall is at its weakest.

recall_q.en: When is post-MI free-wall rupture most likely?

explain_simple.en: Dead muscle is cleared before new scar is laid down; in that gap the wall is soft.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

title.en: Phases of the cardiac cycle (left heart)

text.en: Isovolumic contraction: mitral valve closes (S1); all valves shut; LV pressure rises with no volume change.

explain.en: The ventricle squeezes a closed box, so pressure climbs until it beats aortic pressure.

text.en: Ejection: aortic valve opens when LV pressure exceeds aortic pressure; stroke volume leaves the ventricle.
Isovolumic relaxation: aortic valve closes (S2); all valves shut; LV pressure falls with no volume change.
Rapid filling: mitral valve opens when LV pressure drops below LA pressure; most filling happens here.
Diastasis: slow filling as LA and LV pressures equalise; shortened first when heart rate rises.
Atrial systole: atrial kick adds the last part of filling (the 'a' wave); lost in atrial fibrillation.

summary.en: Two isovolumic phases: all valves closed.
S1 = mitral/tricuspid close; S2 = aortic/pulmonary close.
Atrial kick is lost in AF.

recall_q.en: Name the six phases of the cardiac cycle in order.

recall_a.en: Isovolumic contraction, ejection, isovolumic relaxation, rapid filling, diastasis, atrial systole.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 1 (3 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Dominance = artery giving the PDA; ~70% right-dominant.
AV nodal artery usually from RCA: inferior MI causes AV block.
LV is perfused in diastole; tachycardia worsens ischaemia.
PGE1 keeps the ductus open in duct-dependent lesions.
Post-MI free-wall rupture peaks about 3–7 days.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Standard ECG paper runs at 25 mm/s: one small square is 0.04 s, one large square is 0.20 s, and 10 mm equals 1 mV.

why.en: All intervals and rates are measured by counting squares at this standard speed and gain.

recall_q.en: How long is one large ECG square at 25 mm/s?

explain_simple.en: Five small squares make a big square; 5 × 0.04 s = 0.20 s.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Normal ECG intervals: PR 0.12–0.20 s, QRS under 0.12 s; QT must be corrected for heart rate (QTc).

why.en: A long PR means slow AV conduction, a wide QRS means slow ventricular conduction, and a long QTc raises torsades risk.

recall_q.en: What is the upper limit of a normal PR interval?

explain_simple.en: PR: three to five small squares. QRS: under three small squares.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: On a PA chest X-ray, a cardiothoracic ratio above 0.5 suggests cardiomegaly.

why.en: The AP view magnifies the heart because it lies far from the film, so CTR is judged only on PA films.

recall_q.en: Why is cardiothoracic ratio not judged on an AP film?

recall_a.en: The AP view magnifies the heart.

explain_simple.en: In a PA film the heart sits close to the detector, so its size is true. In AP it is far away and looks bigger.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Global longitudinal strain (GLS) on speckle-tracking echo is normally about −20%; a relative fall over 15% from baseline signals subclinical LV dysfunction.

why.en: GLS falls before ejection fraction, so it detects early damage, for example during cardiotoxic chemotherapy.

recall_q.en: What GLS change suggests subclinical cardiotoxicity?

recall_a.en: A relative fall of more than 15% from baseline.

explain_simple.en: Strain measures how much the muscle shortens. It weakens before EF drops, so it is an early warning.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Fractional flow reserve (FFR) ≤0.80 marks a haemodynamically significant coronary stenosis; for iFR the cut-off is ≤0.89.

why.en: FFR is distal over aortic pressure at maximal hyperaemia, so it shows whether the lesion actually limits flow.

recall_q.en: What FFR value indicates a significant stenosis?

explain_simple.en: If pressure beyond the narrowing is 80% or less of aortic pressure, the narrowing is limiting flow and stenting helps.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: On PET, reduced perfusion with preserved FDG uptake (perfusion–metabolism mismatch) indicates hibernating, viable myocardium.

why.en: Living but under-perfused muscle still uses glucose, so it can recover after revascularisation.

recall_q.en: What PET pattern indicates hibernating myocardium?

explain_simple.en: Low blood flow but still eating glucose means the muscle is alive and asleep, not dead.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: On cardiac MRI, late gadolinium enhancement over 50% of wall thickness predicts little chance of recovery after revascularisation.

why.en: Gadolinium collects in scar; the more transmural the scar, the less living muscle remains.

recall_q.en: What LGE transmurality predicts poor recovery?

explain_simple.en: Bright areas on late MRI are scar. If scar fills over half the wall, opening the artery helps little.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: In pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) measurement, the wedged catheter estimates left atrial pressure.

why.en: With flow stopped by the balloon, the static column links the catheter tip to the left atrium.

recall_q.en: What does pulmonary artery wedge pressure estimate?

explain_simple.en: Blocking a small lung artery lets the catheter 'see' through the lung vessels to the left atrium.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

exam_q.en: A man exercises 7 minutes on the Bruce protocol with 2 mm ST depression and non-limiting angina. Calculate his Duke treadmill score and risk group.

exam_note.en: A question like this can come in the exam.

given.en: Exercise time 7 min, ST deviation 2 mm, angina index 1 (non-limiting).

find.en: Duke treadmill score and risk category.

idea.en: DTS = time − 5 × ST deviation − 4 × angina index.

theory.en: Duke score = minutes − 5×(max ST deviation, mm) − 4×(angina index: 0 none, 1 non-limiting, 2 limiting). ≥+5 low risk; −10 to +4 intermediate; ≤−11 high risk.

why.en: Exercise duration in minutes on the Bruce protocol.
Each mm of ST deviation is weighted by 5.
Non-limiting angina has index 1.
Subtract both penalty terms from time.
Use the standard Duke risk bands.

q.en: Exercise 10 min, 1 mm ST depression, no angina. Score and risk?
Exercise 3 min, 3 mm ST depression, test-limiting angina. Score and risk?

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

exam_q.en: On a regular ECG at 25 mm/s, the R–R interval is 4 large squares. What is the heart rate?

exam_note.en: A question like this can come in the exam.

given.en: Regular rhythm, R–R = 4 large squares, paper speed 25 mm/s.

find.en: Heart rate in beats per minute.

idea.en: 300 large squares pass in one minute.

theory.en: At 25 mm/s, rate = 300 ÷ large squares between R waves, or 1500 ÷ small squares. For irregular rhythms, count QRS in 10 s and multiply by 6.

why.en: One minute is 300 large squares (60 s ÷ 0.2 s).
Simple division.

q.en: R–R interval is 15 small squares. Heart rate?
Irregular rhythm with 13 QRS complexes on a 10-second strip. Heart rate?

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

text.en: Check calibration (10 mm/mV) and speed (25 mm/s); confirm patient details.
Rate: 300 ÷ large squares between R waves, or count QRS in 10 s × 6 if irregular.
Rhythm: is every QRS preceded by a P wave, and is R–R regular?
Axis: leads I and aVF; normal is about −30° to +90°.

explain.en: Both positive means normal axis. Lead I positive, aVF negative: check lead II for left axis deviation.

text.en: Intervals: PR 0.12–0.20 s, QRS under 0.12 s, QTc for rate.
P wave and QRS morphology: atrial enlargement, bundle branch block, hypertrophy, Q waves.
ST segments and T waves: elevation, depression, inversion — map them to a coronary territory.

summary.en: Rate, rhythm, axis, intervals, morphology, ST–T.
Map ST changes to coronary territories.

recall_q.en: List the order of a systematic ECG read.

recall_a.en: Calibration, rate, rhythm, axis, intervals, P/QRS morphology, ST–T.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

say.en: Draw a flat baseline: this is the isoelectric line.
Add a small rounded P wave: atrial depolarisation.
A short flat PR segment, then a small dip (Q), a tall spike (R) and a dip below (S).
Flat ST segment, then a broad rounded T wave: ventricular repolarisation.

recall_prompt.en: Draw a normal ECG complex from memory and label P, Q, R, S and T.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 2 (5 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: ECG: small square 0.04 s, large 0.20 s at 25 mm/s.
CTR above 0.5 on PA film suggests cardiomegaly.
GLS relative fall over 15% = subclinical LV dysfunction.
FFR ≤0.80 (iFR ≤0.89) = significant stenosis.
PET mismatch = hibernating; LGE over 50% = poor recovery.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 3 (2 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is usually autosomal dominant, caused by sarcomere gene variants; MYH7 and MYBPC3 are the commonest.

why.en: Faulty sarcomere proteins make the muscle hypercontractile and disorganised, so it thickens.

recall_q.en: Which two genes most often cause HCM?

explain_simple.en: HCM is a disease of the muscle's motor proteins; the two big culprits code for beta-myosin heavy chain and myosin-binding protein C.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 3 (2 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Familial hypercholesterolaemia is autosomal dominant, most often from LDLR variants (also APOB, PCSK9); heterozygotes are about 1 in 250.

why.en: Fewer working LDL receptors means LDL is cleared slowly, so LDL-C is high from birth.

recall_q.en: Which gene is most commonly mutated in familial hypercholesterolaemia?

explain_simple.en: The liver's LDL 'doors' are broken, so LDL piles up in blood from childhood.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 3 (2 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Long QT triggers by genotype: LQT1 (KCNQ1) exercise or swimming; LQT2 (KCNH2) sudden noise or emotion; LQT3 (SCN5A) sleep or rest.

why.en: Each gene affects a different ion current, so a different situation tips the patient into torsades.

recall_q.en: Which long QT type is triggered by swimming?

explain_simple.en: Think 1-2-3: Exercise, Emotion/noise, rest/sleep.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 3 (2 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Marfan syndrome is caused by FBN1 (fibrillin-1) variants; aortic root dilatation and dissection are the main cardiac risks.

why.en: Defective fibrillin weakens elastic fibres and increases TGF-β signalling in the aortic wall.

recall_q.en: Which gene is mutated in Marfan syndrome?

explain_simple.en: Fibrillin is the scaffold of elastic tissue; when it is faulty the aortic root stretches.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 3 (2 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

learn.en: Inclisiran is a small interfering RNA that silences hepatic PCSK9 synthesis, lowering LDL-C with twice-yearly dosing after loading.

why.en: Less PCSK9 means fewer LDL receptors are destroyed, so the liver clears more LDL.

recall_q.en: How does inclisiran lower LDL?

recall_a.en: siRNA silencing of PCSK9 production in the liver.

explain_simple.en: Antibodies mop up PCSK9 in blood; inclisiran stops the liver making it in the first place.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 1 item 3 (2 marks); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: HCM: autosomal dominant; MYH7 and MYBPC3.
FH: LDLR commonest; heterozygous about 1 in 250.
LQT1 exercise, LQT2 emotion/noise, LQT3 sleep.
Marfan: FBN1; watch aortic root.
Inclisiran: siRNA against PCSK9.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 2 (i); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: STEMI: primary PCI preferred if achievable within 120 min of diagnosis.
NSTE-ACS: use high-sensitivity troponin 0/1-hour algorithm.
DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless high bleeding risk.
High-intensity statin for all; ESC LDL-C goal under 55 mg/dL.
CCS: anti-anginals plus risk control; revascularise refractory or high-risk anatomy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 2 (ii); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Severe AS: AVA under 1.0 cm², mean gradient ≥40 mmHg, Vmax ≥4 m/s.
Symptomatic severe AS needs valve replacement (SAVR or TAVI).
Significant MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm².
PTMC needs favourable anatomy, no LA thrombus, at most mild MR.
Rheumatic disease remains a major cause of MS in India.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 2 (iii); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: VSD is the commonest congenital heart defect.
Tetralogy of Fallot is the commonest cyanotic lesion after infancy.
TGA is the commonest cyanotic lesion presenting in newborns.
Eisenmenger: shunt reverses as pulmonary vascular disease develops.
Duct-dependent lesions: start prostaglandin E1 at once.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 3 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: HFrEF ≤40%, HFmrEF 41–49%, HFpEF ≥50% ejection fraction.
HFrEF pillars: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor.
ADHF profiles: warm/cold perfusion and wet/dry congestion.
IV loop diuretic is first-line for congestion in ADHF.
SGLT2 inhibitors also benefit HFmrEF and HFpEF.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 3 (b); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: ESC/ISH: hypertension is office BP ≥140/90 mmHg.
First-line: ACEi/ARB, calcium channel blocker, thiazide-like diuretic.
Prefer single-pill combinations to improve adherence.
Resistant: uncontrolled on three drugs incl. diuretic; add spironolactone.
Screen for primary aldosteronism, renal artery stenosis, sleep apnoea.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 3 (c); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Vaughan Williams: I Na, II beta, III K, IV Ca channel.
Secondary-prevention ICD after VF or unstable VT without reversible cause.
Primary-prevention ICD: LVEF ≤35% after ≥3 months optimal therapy, NYHA II–III.
Ablation is curative for AVNRT, accessory pathways and typical flutter.
Unstable tachyarrhythmia: synchronised DC cardioversion.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 4 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: HCM: unexplained LV wall ≥15 mm; LVOT obstruction if gradient ≥30 mmHg.
Obstructive HCM: beta-blocker first; avoid vasodilators and dehydration; mavacamten option.
DCM: dilated LV with systolic dysfunction; treat as HFrEF.
ARVC: fibrofatty RV replacement; epsilon wave on ECG.
ATTR amyloid: diagnose with bone scintigraphy; treat with tafamidis.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 5 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Acute pericarditis: 2 of chest pain, rub, ECG changes, effusion.
Treat with NSAID or aspirin plus colchicine to cut recurrence.
Tamponade: Beck's triad and pulsus paradoxus over 10 mmHg.
Constriction: Kussmaul sign, pericardial knock, ventricular interdependence.
Tuberculosis is a major cause of pericardial disease in India.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 6 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Diagnose with modified Duke criteria (2023 Duke-ISCVID update).
Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest organism overall.
Take three blood culture sets before antibiotics.
Surgery for heart failure, uncontrolled infection, or high embolic risk.
Prophylaxis only for high-risk patients before gingival dental procedures.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 6 (b); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

title.en: Prosthetic valves and percutaneous therapy — key points

points.en: Mechanical valves need lifelong warfarin; DOACs are contraindicated.
Typical INR target: 2.5 mechanical aortic, 3.0 mechanical mitral.
Bioprosthetic valves degenerate; valve-in-valve TAVI is an option.
TAVI is favoured in older patients with severe AS.
TEER treats selected severe mitral regurgitation.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 7 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: PH: mean PAP over 20 mmHg at rest (ESC/ERS 2022).
Pre-capillary PH: PAWP ≤15 mmHg and PVR over 2 Wood units.
Group 2 (left heart disease) is the commonest group.
Most PAH: start ERA plus PDE5 inhibitor together.
Positive vasoreactivity test (IPAH): high-dose calcium channel blocker.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 8 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

title.en: Stroke and the heart — key points

points.en: AF is a leading cause of cardioembolic stroke.
IV thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of onset in eligible patients.
Thrombectomy for large-vessel occlusion, selected patients up to 24 hours.
Symptomatic carotid stenosis ≥70%: endarterectomy.
PFO closure for selected patients ≤60 with cryptogenic stroke.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 8 (b); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Stroke risk by CHA₂DS₂-VASc (ESC 2024 uses CHA₂DS₂-VA).
DOACs preferred except mechanical valves or moderate–severe MS.
Rate control: beta-blocker, diltiazem/verapamil, or digoxin.
Early rhythm control reduced CV events (EAST-AFNET 4).
Catheter ablation (PVI) for symptomatic AF; benefits selected HFrEF.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 9 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Good functional capacity (≥4 METs) usually allows surgery without testing.
Revised Cardiac Risk Index estimates perioperative cardiac risk.
Continue existing beta-blockers; do not start high-dose just before surgery.
Defer elective surgery about 6 months after elective PCI, 12 after ACS.
Measure troponin or BNP in higher-risk patients.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 10 (a); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Repair AAA at ≥5.5 cm in men, ≥5.0 cm in women, or fast growth.
Stanford type A dissection: emergency surgery.
Uncomplicated type B: medical therapy; TEVAR if complicated.
Acute dissection: heart rate under 60, systolic 100–120 mmHg.
Marfan: elective root replacement at about 5.0 cm.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 10 (b); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: ABI ≤0.90 diagnoses PAD; over 1.40 means non-compressible arteries.
All patients: antiplatelet therapy and statin.
Low-dose rivaroxaban plus aspirin reduces events (COMPASS, VOYAGER-PAD).
Claudication: supervised exercise; cilostazol (avoid in heart failure).
Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia needs revascularisation.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 10 (c); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

title.en: Diabetes, lipids and CVD — key points

points.en: T2DM with ASCVD: SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA with proven CV benefit.
Very high risk: LDL-C under 55 mg/dL and ≥50% reduction (ESC).
Statin first, then ezetimibe, then PCSK9 inhibitor.
Measure lipoprotein(a) at least once in adulthood.
Icosapent ethyl lowers events with high triglycerides on statin.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 10 (c); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

title.en: Pregnancy and heart disease — key points

points.en: mWHO IV (avoid pregnancy): PAH, LVEF under 30%, severe symptomatic AS.
ACEi, ARB and ARNI are contraindicated in pregnancy.
Warfarin embryopathy risk is higher above 5 mg/day in first trimester.
Peripartum cardiomyopathy: HF late pregnancy or postpartum, LVEF under 45%.
Bromocriptine may be considered in peripartum cardiomyopathy.

cards.source: Kerala PSC detailed syllabus, Assistant Professor (Cardiology), Module 10 (d); Standard reference: Braunwald's Heart Disease 12th ed. (chapter/page not yet verified)

points.en: Use Wells or Geneva score; D-dimer to exclude non-high probability.
CT pulmonary angiography is the first-line imaging test.
High-risk (shock) PE: systemic thrombolysis.
DOACs are first-line anticoagulants, for at least 3 months.
Stratify normotensive patients with sPESI, RV function and troponin.

q.en: Coronary dominance is determined by the artery that gives rise to the:

explain.en: Dominance is defined by the origin of the PDA.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Free-wall rupture after myocardial infarction is most likely at:

explain.en: Necrotic muscle is cleared before scar forms, so the wall is weakest at 3–7 days.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Digoxin toxicity is precipitated most by:

explain.en: Potassium competes with digoxin at the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase; low potassium increases binding.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Fractional flow reserve indicating a haemodynamically significant stenosis is:

explain.en: FFR ≤0.80 marks a functionally significant lesion.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Duke treadmill score for 9 min exercise, 1 mm ST depression and no angina:

explain.en: 9 − 5×1 − 4×0 = +4 (intermediate risk).

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Hibernating myocardium on PET shows:

options.en: Matched reduction of perfusion and FDG

explain.en: Reduced perfusion with preserved glucose use = viable, hibernating myocardium.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Long QT syndrome type 1 is classically triggered by:

explain.en: LQT1 (KCNQ1): exercise, especially swimming.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Inclisiran lowers LDL-C by:

explain.en: Inclisiran is an siRNA that stops hepatic PCSK9 production.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: On a regular ECG the R–R interval is 3 large squares. The heart rate is:

explain.en: 300 ÷ 3 = 100 beats/min.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: The commonest gene implicated in familial hypercholesterolaemia is:

explain.en: LDLR variants cause most FH.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: In STEMI, primary PCI is preferred over fibrinolysis when it can be done within how long of diagnosis?

explain.en: ESC: primary PCI if expected diagnosis-to-wire time is 120 minutes or less.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: ESC LDL-C goal for a patient after acute coronary syndrome is:

explain.en: Very-high-risk patients, including post-ACS, target LDL-C under 55 mg/dL with at least 50% reduction.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Which finding defines severe aortic stenosis?

explain.en: Severe AS: Vmax ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40 mmHg, AVA under 1.0 cm².

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: A contraindication to percutaneous transmitral commissurotomy (PTMC) is:

explain.en: PTMC needs no LA thrombus and at most mild MR; LA thrombus risks embolism.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: The commonest congenital heart defect is:

explain.en: VSD is the commonest congenital heart defect (excluding bicuspid aortic valve).

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: The commonest cyanotic congenital heart lesion presenting in the newborn period is:

explain.en: TGA presents in newborns; Tetralogy is the commonest cyanotic lesion after infancy.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) has an LVEF of:

explain.en: HFrEF ≤40%, HFmrEF 41–49%, HFpEF ≥50%.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Which is NOT one of the four pillars of HFrEF therapy?

explain.en: The four pillars are ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blocker, MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor. Digoxin is add-on only.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Resistant hypertension is BP above target despite three drugs including a diuretic. The preferred fourth drug is:

explain.en: PATHWAY-2 supports spironolactone as the fourth-line drug.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Per ESC/ISH, hypertension is diagnosed at an office BP of:

explain.en: ESC/ISH define hypertension as office BP ≥140/90 mmHg.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: In the Vaughan Williams classification, class III drugs act mainly by blocking:

explain.en: Class I Na, II beta, III K, IV Ca.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Primary-prevention ICD is indicated when LVEF stays at or below what value after 3 months of optimal therapy (NYHA II–III)?

explain.en: LVEF ≤35% after ≥3 months of optimal medical therapy.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in HCM is defined by a gradient of at least:

explain.en: LVOTO is a gradient ≥30 mmHg; ≥50 mmHg is usually the threshold for invasive therapy.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: An epsilon wave on ECG is characteristic of:

explain.en: Epsilon waves reflect delayed RV activation in ARVC.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Colchicine is added to NSAIDs in acute pericarditis mainly to:

explain.en: Colchicine roughly halves recurrence (COPE, ICAP trials).

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Kussmaul sign is most typical of:

explain.en: JVP rising on inspiration is a classic sign of constriction; tamponade shows pulsus paradoxus.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: The commonest organism causing infective endocarditis overall is:

explain.en: S. aureus is now the leading cause in most series.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Antibiotic prophylaxis against endocarditis is recommended for high-risk patients before:

explain.en: Prophylaxis only for high-risk patients undergoing gingival or periapical dental work.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Which anticoagulant is contraindicated with a mechanical heart valve?

explain.en: DOACs (RE-ALIGN with dabigatran) are contraindicated in mechanical valves.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Typical INR target for a mechanical mitral valve is:

explain.en: Mechanical mitral ~3.0; mechanical aortic ~2.5 (adjusted for valve and risk factors).

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: ESC/ERS 2022 define pulmonary hypertension as resting mean PAP above:

explain.en: The threshold was lowered from ≥25 to >20 mmHg in 2022.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: The commonest group of pulmonary hypertension is:

explain.en: PH due to left heart disease is the commonest.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: IV thrombolysis for acute ischaemic stroke is given in eligible patients within how many hours of onset?

explain.en: Thrombolysis up to 4.5 h; thrombectomy for LVO in selected patients up to 24 h.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Carotid endarterectomy is clearly indicated for symptomatic carotid stenosis of:

explain.en: Symptomatic ≥70% stenosis gains most from endarterectomy.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: DOACs are NOT recommended in AF with:

explain.en: Mechanical valves and moderate-to-severe MS need warfarin.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: The EAST-AFNET 4 trial showed that early rhythm control:

explain.en: Early rhythm control reduced the composite of CV death, stroke and HF/ACS admissions.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: A patient with good functional capacity can usually proceed to non-cardiac surgery without further testing if able to do at least:

explain.en: ≥4 METs (e.g. climbing two flights of stairs) predicts low risk.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: After PCI for acute coronary syndrome, elective non-cardiac surgery should ideally be deferred for about:

explain.en: About 6 months after elective PCI and 12 months after ACS, for DAPT.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Stanford type A aortic dissection is treated with:

explain.en: Type A involves the ascending aorta and needs emergency surgery.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Elective repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm in men is recommended at a diameter of:

explain.en: Men ≥5.5 cm, women ≥5.0 cm, or rapid growth.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: An ankle-brachial index above 1.40 indicates:

explain.en: ABI >1.40 means calcified, non-compressible vessels; use toe-brachial index.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Cilostazol for claudication should be avoided in:

explain.en: PDE3 inhibitors are contraindicated in heart failure.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Lipoprotein(a) should be measured:

explain.en: ESC/EAS advise measuring Lp(a) at least once in every adult.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: In a patient on maximum statin with LDL-C above goal, the next drug usually added is:

explain.en: Statin first, then ezetimibe, then a PCSK9 inhibitor.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Which drug group is contraindicated in pregnancy?

explain.en: ACEi, ARB and ARNI are fetotoxic.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Which condition is modified WHO class IV, where pregnancy is advised against?

explain.en: PAH, LVEF under 30% and severe symptomatic AS are mWHO IV.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: The first-line imaging test for suspected pulmonary embolism is:

explain.en: CTPA is first-line; echo is used bedside in shocked patients who cannot be moved.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)

q.en: Systemic thrombolysis is indicated in pulmonary embolism with:

explain.en: High-risk PE with shock or persistent hypotension needs reperfusion, usually thrombolysis.

questions.source: Practice — exam pattern (not from a past paper)
